title: Vendor onboarding: pricing, KMS keying, and SLA acceptance sync
header: Date: 2026-12-29 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 1h04m | Recording: Fireflies.ai automated capture. Attendees: Redwood AE+SE+CSM; Trellis procurement/legal/infosec/platform. Goal: align on MSA/DPA redlines, KMS key ownership, egress pricing, and next steps to move pilot to pilot-to-prod approval.
summary: High-level alignment reached on KMS keying options (customer-managed vs Redwood-hosted with HSM), pricing band for hosted inference during pilot, and a path for SLA carveouts. Legal to provide two prioritized MSA/DPA redlines by next Tuesday; Redwood to supply a KMS architecture diagram and escrow/kms SOP. Action items focus on security docs and a short bench test to validate egress measurements.
topics: Customer-managed KMS vs Redwood HSM options
Pricing bands and egress fees for pilot vs committed capacity
SLA language (SLO targets, credits, uptime measurement)
next_steps: Redwood to send KMS architecture diagram and HSM whitepaper (Alex) - by 2027-01-03
Trellis legal to send prioritized MSA/DPA redlines (Karen) - by 2027-01-02
Schedule 30-min bench test for egress/pricing measurement (Priya + Sean) - week of 2027-01-04
Agree on pilot pricing band and sign pilot addendum (Dana + Alex) - target 2027-01-10

Alex Chen|Send KMS architecture diagram, HSM whitepaper, and SOC2 scope doc|2027-01-03

transcript: 00:00 Alex Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for joining on short notice um we've got about an hour, so we'll try to move quick. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. 00:12 Dana Park: Thanks Alex, Dana here in procurement, we've got legal and infosec on the line to go through the MSA/DPA redlines and then KMS specifics. 00:20 Karen Liu: hi all, Karen from Legal at Trellis. We circulated the baseline MSA yesterday, there are a handful of DPA items we want to prioritize. 00:30 Priya Singh: Hey all, Priya, SE. I'll try to keep the tech answers succinct — KMS, HSM, egress, that sort of thing. 00:38 Ibrahim Saleh: Ibrahim, Infosec. Main concerns: customer key custody, audit log tamper-evidence, and data residency for EU customers. 00:46 Marco Ruiz: Marco, CSM — I'll be tracking timelines and onboarding tasks. 00:50 Alex Chen: Great. Quick agenda: legal timeline, KMS options (customer-managed key in their KMS, vs Redwood-hosted HSM with bring-your-own-key modes), pricing on egress and inference tokens for pilot, and SLA language. 01:05 Dana Park: On pricing we need a pilot band and a committed band. Procurement can't sign off unless costs are predictable. 01:13 Priya Singh: Totally. For pilot we normally offer a hosted rate-card with a cap, e.g., X tokens per second baseline and a measured egress fee; for committed capacity (Dedicated) we have reserved pricing and different egress treatment. 01:27 Sean O'Neill: Could you define 'egress' here? Is it outbound model artifacts or tokenized responses? We bill differently if it's model download vs inference responses. 01:34 Priya Singh: Good call. For Trellis's use case — mostly async text generation and embeddings — egress is measured as response payload bytes leaving Redwood across the public network; model weights never leave unless you're taking a model snapshot. 01:48 Ibrahim Saleh: So model weights remain in Redwood infra unless we request a private deployment. We're evaluating Private (VPC) vs Hosted. Private would keep everything inside our VPC, correct? 01:59 Priya Singh: Yes. Private (we sometimes say Redwood Private) can be customer VPC or on-prem package; you can bring network controls. In that model you can elect customer-managed KMS with key material in your KMS, or Redwood can integrate with your HSM provider. 02:12 Karen Liu: Legally, our preference is customer-managed keys for data at rest encryption; DPA needs to show that Trellis controls keys. 02:21 Alex Chen: Understood. Technically we support two modes: 1) Customer-managed keys where we never see plaintext key material — we integrate via KMIP or cloud KMS, and keys are used to unwrap at the edge; 2) Redwood-hosted HSM where keys are in our HSM with strict access controls and audit trail. 02:39 Sean O'Neill: Any difference in latency between the two? We worry about tail latency if every token requires a KMS hop. 02:45 Priya Singh: We handle KMS ops asynchronously; key unwrap happens at model load time and we keep keys cached in an encrypted key-cache; per-token crypto ops are not performed. There might be a small hit at session start, but not per-token. 03:00 Ibrahim Saleh: Cache makes sense but what about key residency and split-knowledge? We need documented split-key proofs. 03:07 Priya Singh: We can do split-key modes with envelope encryption; Redwood supports envelope with your KMS as the root of trust. We'll share the architecture doc. 03:15 Karen Liu: We'll need SOC2 scope and whether Redwood's audit logs include token-level tracing for requests originating from Trellis. 03:23 Alex Chen: We have SOC2 Type II, ISO in progress; our Console exposes per-route logs and token-level cost breakdown, and we can provide audit exports. We'll attach SOC2 report and a sample audit export. 03:36 Dana Park: On MSA redlines — we flagged indemnity, data deletion timelines, and SLA credits. Can you confirm your SLA targets and how credits are calculated? 03:45 Alex Chen: Typical SLA for Hosted is 99.9% uptime with latency p90 targets; Dedicated has a higher SLO and contractual credit schedule. Credits are prorated for downtime windows measured by our monitoring. We can draft language that defines measurement windows, incident notification, and dispute process. 04:03 Karen Liu: We want SLOs that include availability for the API and for the keying service separately, because if KMS goes down it affects availability even if runtime is healthy. 04:14 Priya Singh: Makes sense. We can split SLOs: 1) Serving runtime (model inference) availability, 2) Keying service availability. Keying service has a higher redundancy profile if you choose Redwood HSM, but if you choose customer KMS, the SLO partly depends on your KMS-provider. 04:35 Sean O'Neill: For pilot, are we expected to provision our own KMS or can we evaluate both modes? 04:41 Alex Chen: You can evaluate both. For the bench test we'd suggest Redwood-hosted with customer-managed keys simulated, and then test actual customer-managed KMS in a later test. 04:50 Priya Singh: For egress bench, we'll run a 2-hour synthetic load using representative prompts to measure bytes per inference and average latency under your expected concurrency. 04:58 Dana Park: Pricing: Trellis needs a capped pilot spend. Can Redwood provide a pilot addendum with a not-to-exceed? 05:04 Alex Chen: Yes — we typically do a pilot addendum with a capped not-to-exceed amount and a defined scope. For production we'll propose either hosted pay-as-you-go or Dedicated reserved pricing. 05:15 Ibrahim Saleh: Any encryption-in-transit specifics? TLS mutual auth? 05:19 Priya Singh: We support mTLS, client certs, and token-based auth. For Private we can do VPC peering or private link. 05:27 Karen Liu: Data residency for EU customers — do you offer region pinning and EU-only processing? 05:31 Alex Chen: Yes, regional routing and model variants pinned to EU regions; we can guarantee processing in region via VPC/private deployment. We'll note that in the DPA. 05:41 Dana Park: Regarding the DPA, we still need clarity on subprocessors — does Redwood use any third-party logging or tracing vendors? 05:48 Marco Ruiz: We use a small set of vendor services for observability and analytics; those are listed in our subprocessor registry. We'll include the current registry in the package we send. 05:58 Karen Liu: Also want a clause on data deletion — standard is 30 days, but some of our data is regulated; we might ask for 7-day deletion for certain classes. 06:08 Priya Singh: We can support shorter retention windows for committed customers; need to confirm for pilot whether that impacts metrics. 06:18 Sean O'Neill: One more platform question — if we choose Dedicated, can we run a quantized model variant to reduce cost, or does that change fidelity materially? 06:28 Priya Singh: We support quantized model variants; we can recommend a q4_0 or q2_k variant and provide evals. In most generative workloads fidelity drop is small but we should run evals on your prompt sets. 06:41 Ibrahim Saleh: Any export control flags? We have some customers in sensitive sectors. 06:46 Alex Chen: We have export controls review in our legal playbook and can add restricted-country lists to routing rules. 06:54 Dana Park: Ok, this is helpful. To recap — Trellis legal sends prioritized redlines; Redwood sends KMS arch and SOC2; schedule bench test; Redwood to propose pilot addendum with not-to-exceed. 07:07 Karen Liu: Correct. Also we'll want the subprocessor registry and a sample audit export. 07:12 Marco Ruiz: Noted. I'll own the project timeline and keep a tracker in the shared folder. 07:18 Sean O'Neill: Quick clarification on bench test — can we get a script up front so we can provision ephemeral infra accordingly? 07:24 Priya Singh: Absolutely, I'll share the script and expected traffic profile. 07:28 Dana Park: Great, thanks all. If legal signs off on the pilot addendum we'll move to execution. 07:35 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll send the materials and follow up with calendar invites for the bench slot. 07:39 (crosstalk) Karen Liu: thanks, bye. 07:41 Alex Chen: Bye everyone, end recording.
notes: Audio had moderate interruptions during cross-geo network handoff; some proper nouns mis-transcribed (e.g., HSM vendor names)
Customer emphasized key custody and split-key envelope encryption; legal cares about shortening deletion windows for regulated datasets
